messages:
Alex W: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel heuristic push I see p99 spikes on some routes. Spike is concentrated in the prefill stage, decode p99 looks stable. Anyone else seeing this? :eyes:
perf-bot: quick snapshot:
```
model: redwood-open-7b
cohort: chat-long-history
metrics:
  prefill: p50=18ms p95=62ms p99=142ms
  decode: p50=4ms p95=12ms p99=20ms
kernel_selector: matmul_v2 preferred for batch<8
kv_cache_miss_rate: 0.18
gpu_util: 72% (avg)
microbatch_window_ms: 12
```
Jia N: Hmm that p99 delta on prefill is concerning (142ms). Pre-fill doing attention + KV copy; if kernel selector picked a non-fused attention kernel for certain seq lengths we can blow tail. Did the selector rule change for depth/seq > 1024?
Mike R: I traced a few slow requests. KV copy path shows repeated cache misses causing re-eviction thrash. Miss rate jumps from 3% -> 18% for the long-history cohort. Trace snippet: `rbx-trace get 0x8f2b3c --span=prefill` shows repeated `kv_copy: allocate -> dealloc` patterns.
Sara L: We flipped the heuristic to prefer matmul_v2 on the canary to reduce memory footprint for tiny batches. For longer seqs it seems to pick matmul_v2 even when fused_attention would be faster. Might be the sequence-length threshold is too low.
Alex W: Can we A/B this quickly? Two canaries: 1) batch cap=4, microbatch_window=8ms (current canary), 2) batch cap=16, microbatch_window=20ms, and run warm/cold KV cache tests. Watch prefill p95/p99.
Priya: Running the A/B is fine but remember throughput vs SLO tradeoff: larger microbatches will help throughput but may hurt p95 for single-request latency. Suggest we also measure average token/sec and request tail.
Mike R: Quick numbers from a local run (warm KV vs cold KV) — rough:
- microbatch=4: prefill p95=58ms p99=130ms, decode p95=11ms p99=19ms, kv_miss=16%
- microbatch=8: prefill p95=52ms p99=98ms, decode p95=12ms p99=22ms, kv_miss=9%
- microbatch=16: prefill p95=49ms p99=76ms, decode p95=15ms p99=34ms, kv_miss=3%
Observations: larger microbatch reduced prefill p99 and kv misses but decode p99 increases a bit (due to batching queuing).
Jia N: Also saw kernel fallback entries in the runtime log for the slow traces: `kernel_select: fallback_attention_slow -> fused_attention_v1` which indicates the selector tried matmul_v2 then fell back. Fallback cost shows up at prefill tail. Log snippet:
```
[2026-03-16T22:41:02Z] kernel_select: chosen=matmul_v2 seq=1200 batch=6
[2026-03-16T22:41:02Z] kernel_exec: FAIL fastpath -> fallback to fused_attention_v1 (120ms extra)
```
Sara L: That fallback is the smoking gun. We should adjust selector to avoid risky picks that cause fallback for seq>1024 or when kv_miss_rate>5%. Maybe add a cheap cost-estimate pass based on seq_len and kv_cache_state before choosing.
Alex W: Action items (assign):
1) Revert the matmul_v2 preference on canary routes where seq_len>1024 (Sara)
2) Run systematic microbatch sweep (4/8/16) with warm/cold KV and produce p50/p95/p99 breakdown for prefill+decode (Mike)
3) Emit per-route kv_miss_rate and kernel_fallback_counter metrics to grafana (Jia)
4) Add a lightweight selector pre-check using seq_len + kv_miss hint to avoid known-fallback combos (Priya/Sara)
Please post results as short tables in this thread.
perf-bot: benchmark queue created: https://bench.redwood.internal/q/9a7f — test config includes `--kv-warm` and `--kv-cold` runs.
Sara L: :thumbsup: I'll take 1 and help Priya with 4. Will kick off canary rollback and post logs. Expect updates within 3 hours.
Mike R: Kicking off the sweep now, will attach run summary when done. Preliminary note: decode latency increase at microbatch=16 looks due to queueing delay; we should explore adaptive microbatch window (increase for cold-kv workloads).
Alex W: Thanks all. If anyone sees unexpected p99 regressions beyond these configs, ping here and escalate to oncall.
deploy-bot: canary traffic reconfigured for route `chat-long-history` -> matmul_v2 pref disabled (id: deploy-7732)
Sara L: Rollback complete, initial canary results look like prefill p99 dropped from ~140ms -> ~88ms. Sharing detailed numbers in follow-up.
